title: Differential reporting with residency-aware redaction & webhook delivery
creator: Jonah Rivera
description:
Background: Customers need scheduled compliance exports (PDF/CSV) and dashboard snapshots that respect tenant data residency and retention settings. Current export features produce full snapshots and lack fine-grained redaction rules or delivery guarantees that enterprise customers require for audits.

Goal: Deliver a scheduled differential export capability that produces compact, signed bundles (full snapshot + delta) and supports residency-aware redaction and delivery via webhook or S3 with retry/SLA controls. The feature should integrate with the Console dashboards and provide downloadable artifacts plus an audit manifest.

User stories:
- As a platform owner, I want daily differential CSV extracts for each tenant so I only transfer changed records to our archival store.
- As a compliance officer, I want exported PDFs to automatically mask or omit fields when data residency rules prohibit export from certain regions.
- As an SRE, I want webhook delivery with exponential backoff and SLA alerts so external systems can reliably ingest exported bundles.

Scope (in):
- Scheduled exports (cron-like) producing full snapshot + delta (differential) in CSV and PDF formats.
- Residency-aware export pipeline: configurable per-tenant redaction policies (mask/remove), region pinning for export origin, and residency routing.
- Delivery targets: webhook endpoints (with HMAC signatures), S3-compatible endpoints (TLS + SSE), and console download.
- Signed manifests for each bundle containing provenance (timestamp, tenant, originating region, retention TTL, SHA256 checksums).
- Dashboard tiles showing export status, last successful delivery, and bytes transferred.

Non-goals (out of this ticket):
- Full e-discovery tools or complex journal replays.
- Per-record cryptographic sealing beyond bundle manifests.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Admins can create scheduled export subscriptions scoped to a tenant with options: format (CSV/PDF), cadence, residency enforcement level (strict/remove/mask), and delivery target (webhook/s3/console).
2) Exports produce a delta file containing only changed records since the last successful export and a full snapshot on first run.
3) Residency rules are enforced: fields marked by the residency policy are either redacted (mask) or omitted (remove) from exported artifacts according to the tenant's policy.
4) Each bundle includes a manifest.json (human-readable) with SHA256 checksums, originating region, retention TTL, and an HMAC signature header when delivered to webhooks.
5) Delivery subsystem retries transient failures with backoff and surfaces failures in Console alerts; SLA breach triggers an incident notification.
6) Dashboard surfaces per-subscription history (last 30 days), bytes, and delivery success rate.
7) Security review sign-off completed and KMS configured for S3 SSE and manifest signing.

Technical approach (high level):
- Export worker runs in the regional export pool to honor residency constraints; workers leverage existing snapshotting and CDC streams to compute diffs.
- A residency enforcement layer applies per-tenant redaction rules before bundling and writes artifacts to regional object store.
- Delivery service handles signed webhook posts (HMAC) and S3 uploads with per-tenant encryption keys. Retries use exponential backoff and a circuit-breaker to avoid repeated failures.
- Console backend stores metadata and aggregates metrics for dashboarding.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal customers only, residency=off, limited to CSV diffs.
- Beta: residency policies enabled, PDF export and webhook delivery to allowlisted endpoints.
- GA: tenant self-serve in Console, SLA options and region pinning.

Compliance and security considerations:
- All artifacts written for regionally-restricted tenants must remain in-region.
- Use KMS-managed keys per-tenant when available; fall back to platform key with audit trail.
- Maintain retention TTL in manifest; automated purge job must honor tenant retention.

Metrics to track:
- Exports/day, average bundle size, delivery success rate, mean time to first successful delivery, number of residency enforcement violations (zero target).

2026-02-22 - Engineering feasibility review (ENG-18277): confirmed CDC-based diff approach is viable; potential perf hotspots around PDF rendering for large snapshots. Action: ENG to prototype diff pipeline. Owner: Arjun Patel.

2026-02-26 - Design feedback: add explicit UX for redaction preview in Console so tenants can verify outputs before enabling. Designer: Sofia Alvarez. PRD updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/COMP-EXPORTS/differential-report-spec.

2026-03-01 - Security review kickoff: security to evaluate KMS key-per-tenant model and webhook signing. Security owner: Priya Nambiar. Requested threat model and replay protection for webhook endpoints.

2026-03-03 - Implementation note: prototype branch created (github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw/compare/feat/differential-exports). ENG estimate refined to 5 pts; need infra work to expose regional object stores to export workers (ENG-19654).

2026-03-04 - PM decision: prioritize CSV differential exports for Beta and enable residency redaction; PDF rendering will follow in the same release but gated behind performance tests. Evelyn Park assigned as PM owner.
2026-03-04 - QA plan: create test tenants with mixed residency flags and synthetic change streams; include fuzz tests for redaction rules and webhook replay resistance. QA lead: Carlos Mendes.
